# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Guo_2022_ciprofloxacin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Guo_2022_ciprofloxacin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-022-01114-5> (open access)

# Population

Guo et al. (2022) pooled individual data from three prospective Dutch ICU
studies of intravenous ciprofloxacin: 1094 total plasma concentrations from
140 critically ill adults. Study 1 (Erasmus MC and Maasstad Hospital,
Rotterdam; 42 patients, 204 samples) was previously published as Abdulla 2020
(the EXPAT study; see `Abdulla_2020_ciprofloxacin`), study 2 (Radboud UMC,
Nijmegen; 39 patients, 531 samples) as Gieling 2020, and study 3 (Amsterdam
UMC location VUmc, the Right Dose Right Now study; 59 patients, 359 samples)
was unpublished. Patients were 66% male, median age 67 years (IQR 59-74),
weight 80 kg (IQR 69-93), MDRD eGFR 59 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR 37-96), albumin
25 g/L and SOFA score 10; 8% were on continuous veno-venous hemofiltration
(source Table 1). Most patients received 400 mg twice or three times daily as
30-60 min infusions; study 3 also used model-based individualized dosing.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Guo_2022_ciprofloxacin")()$population`.

Age, sex, serum creatinine, eGFR, albumin, SOFA score and CVVH were screened in
a stepwise covariate search. Only eGFR on clearance was retained, on top of
the a priori allometric weight scaling of all four structural parameters. The
screened covariates are recorded in the model's `covariatesDataExcluded`
metadata.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(14.7 L/h) | Table 2, final model; Eq. 3 |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(61.2 L) | Table 2, final model; Eq. 4 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(44.9 L/h) | Table 2, final model; Eq. 5 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(71.6 L) | Table 2, final model; Eq. 6 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_q` | fixed 0.75 | Methods 2.2.2 (a priori allometry); Eqs. 3 and 5 |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | fixed 1 | Methods 2.2.2; Eqs. 4 and 6 |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.008 per mL/min/1.73 m^2 | Table 2 'eGFR on CL (linear)'; Eq. 3 |
| eGFR centre 58.64 mL/min/1.73 m^2 | n/a | Eq. 3; Results 3.1 (median eGFR) |
| Reference weight 70 kg | n/a | Eqs. 3-6 |
| `etalcl` | 0.2011 | Table 2, IIV CL 47.2% -> log(1 + 0.472^2) |
| `etalvc` | 0.3172 | Table 2, IIV V1 61.1% -> log(1 + 0.611^2) |
| `etalvp` | 0.1981 | Table 2, IIV V2 46.8% -> log(1 + 0.468^2) |
| `etaiov_cl_1` ... `etaiov_cl_7` | 0.01833 | Table 2, IOV CL 13.6% -> log(1 + 0.136^2); 24-h occasions, Methods 2.2.1 |
| `propSd` (study 2) | 0.137 | Table 2, Prop Study2 13.7% |
| `propSd_expat`, `addSd_expat` (study 1) | 0.175, 0.151 mg/L | Table 2, Prop Study1 17.5%, Add Study1 0.151 mg/L |
| `propSd_rdrn` (study 3) | 0.245 | Table 2, Prop Study3 24.5% |
| Two-compartment model, first-order elimination | n/a | Results 3.1 |
| `cl <- ... * (1 + e_crcl_cl * (CRCL - 58.64)) * exp(etalcl + iov_cl)` | n/a | Eq. 3 |

# Typical-patient profiles

The typical patient of Equations 3-6 weighs 70 kg and has eGFR
58.64 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Profiles below are for 400 mg every 8 h given as a
30-min infusion, with the random effects removed, across the eGFR range of the
pooled cohort.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Guo_2022_ciprofloxacin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

typ_subj <- tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  WT = 70,
  CRCL = c(20, 58.64, 100, 140),
  STUDY_EXPAT = 0,
  STUDY_RDRN = 0,
  OCC = 1
)
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  typ_subj |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 8, 16)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 400, rate = 800),
  typ_subj |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_events) |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(CRCL))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (h)", y = "Ciprofloxacin (mg/L)",
    colour = "eGFR\n(mL/min/1.73 m^2)",
    title = "Typical 70-kg patient, 400 mg q8h (30-min infusion)"
  )
```

The clearance of the typical patient must equal the printed 14.7 L/h, and the
eGFR factor must follow Equation 3 exactly (these are typical-value checks with
no random draws, so they are tight):

```{r typical-check}
cl_typ <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(CRCL) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(cl_eq3 = 14.7 * (1 + 0.008 * (CRCL - 58.64)))
knitr::kable(cl_typ, digits = 3, caption = "Typical CL (70 kg) against Equation 3.")
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_typ$cl[cl_typ$CRCL == 58.64] - 14.7) < 1e-6,
  all(abs(cl_typ$cl - cl_typ$cl_eq3) < 1e-6)
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The source data are not public. Each study arm below draws 200 patients whose
body weight and eGFR are log-normal with the per-study median and interquartile
range of Table 1 (log-scale SD = log(Q3/Q1) / 1.349), truncated to
40-150 kg and 5-200 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The study indicators select each study's
residual error; they have no effect on the PK parameters, so differences in
exposure between the simulated arms come only from their covariate
distributions.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2022)
n_arm <- 200

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study, ~wt_med, ~wt_q1, ~wt_q3, ~gfr_med, ~gfr_q1, ~gfr_q3, ~STUDY_EXPAT, ~STUDY_RDRN,
  "Study 1", 80, 64, 90, 58.5, 31.75, 101.75, 1, 0,
  "Study 2", 80, 66, 98.5, 67, 39, 93, 0, 0,
  "Study 3", 80, 70.75, 93, 56.5, 37.75, 93.75, 0, 1
)

make_arm <- function(a, n, id_offset) {
  tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    study = a$study,
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(a$wt_med), log(a$wt_q3 / a$wt_q1) / 1.349)), 40), 150),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(a$gfr_med), log(a$gfr_q3 / a$gfr_q1) / 1.349)), 5), 200),
    STUDY_EXPAT = a$STUDY_EXPAT,
    STUDY_RDRN = a$STUDY_RDRN
  )
}
subjects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(arms[i, ], n_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm)
}))

# 400 mg q8h as a 30-min infusion over the first 24 h (the paper's simulation
# regimen, Methods 2.3.2); the whole window is occasion 1.
events <- bind_rows(
  subjects |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 8, 16)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 400, rate = 800),
  subjects |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = 1L) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

subjects |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `WT median (kg)` = median(WT),
    `eGFR median` = median(CRCL),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated covariates by study arm.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "study") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r vpc}
sim |>
  group_by(study, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~study) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (h)", y = "Ciprofloxacin (mg/L)",
    title = "Median and 90% interval, 400 mg q8h, first 24 h"
  )
```

## Study-specific residual error

The residual error switches by study. Comparing the simulated observation
(`sim`) with the individual prediction (`Cc`) recovers each study's error
model; the proportional component is checked on concentrations above
2 mg/L, where study 1's additive 0.151 mg/L contributes little.

```{r ruv-check}
ruv <- sim |>
  mutate(rel = (sim - Cc) / Cc) |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(
    `SD of (sim - Cc)/Cc, Cc > 2 mg/L` = sd(rel[Cc > 2]),
    `SD of (sim - Cc), Cc < 0.5 mg/L` = sd((sim - Cc)[Cc > 0 & Cc < 0.5]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(`Table 2 proportional` = c(0.175, 0.137, 0.245))
knitr::kable(ruv, digits = 3)

# Proportional SD at high Cc: study 1 additionally carries the additive term
# (0.151 / 2 = 0.076 at the 2 mg/L floor), so it is checked only for being
# at least its proportional SD; studies 2 and 3 are pure proportional.
stopifnot(
  abs(ruv[[2]][2] / 0.137 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(ruv[[2]][3] / 0.245 - 1) < 0.15,
  ruv[[2]][1] > 0.175 * 0.9
)
```

# Replicate Figure 4: AUC24 and target attainment

Guo 2022 simulated 400 mg t.i.d. over the first 24 h from posterior samples of
each patient's PK parameters and reported a mean AUC24 of 47.7, 47.6 and
58 mg h/L for studies 1, 2 and 3 (SD 22.8-25.8), and a probability of target
attainment (AUC24 / MIC >= 125) at MIC 0.5 mg/L of 21%, 18% and 38%. The
packaged model carries no study effect on PK, so the study differences in
Figure 4 (which come from the study-specific posterior distributions, Table 3)
cannot be reproduced; the comparison below is made against the
patient-weighted pooled values (42, 39 and 59 patients).

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, study)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | study + id)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, study)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | study + id)

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

auc24 <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, study, auc24 = PPORRES)
```

```{r figure-4a}
# Replicates Figure 4a of Guo 2022 (AUC24 box plot by study).
ggplot(auc24, aes(study, auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "AUC24 (mg h/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Guo 2022 (simulated virtual cohort)."
  )
```

```{r nca-compare}
w <- c(42, 39, 59)
published <- tibble(
  group = "Pooled (patient-weighted)",
  auclast = sum(w * c(47.7, 47.6, 58)) / sum(w)
)
simulated <- tibble(group = "Pooled (patient-weighted)", auclast = mean(auc24$auc24))
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Mean AUC0-24 after 400 mg q8h: simulated vs. Guo 2022 (Results 3.2.2).")

auc24 |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(auc24), sd = sd(auc24), median = median(auc24), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(`published mean` = c(47.7, 47.6, 58)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated AUC0-24 (mg h/L) by study arm.")
```

```{r figure-4b}
# Replicates Figure 4b of Guo 2022. Published pooled PTA is the
# patient-weighted mean of the three study curves; the 0.5 mg/L values are
# printed in Results 3.2.2, the others are read from Figure 4b.
mics <- c(0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1)
pta_pub <- tibble(
  mic = mics,
  s1 = c(100, 99, 73, 21, 1),
  s2 = c(100, 100, 75, 18, 1),
  s3 = c(100, 99, 90, 38, 2)
) |>
  mutate(published = (42 * s1 + 39 * s2 + 59 * s3) / 140)
pta_sim <- tibble(mic = mics) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(simulated = 100 * mean(auc24$auc24 / mic >= 125)) |>
  ungroup()
pta <- left_join(pta_pub |> select(mic, published), pta_sim, by = "mic")
pta |>
  mutate(mic = format(mic)) |>
  dplyr::rename("MIC (mg/L)" = mic, "Published PTA (%)" = published, "Simulated PTA (%)" = simulated) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Pooled PTA (%), AUC24/MIC >= 125.")

pta |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(published, simulated), names_to = "source", values_to = "PTA") |>
  ggplot(aes(mic, PTA, colour = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4b of Guo 2022 (pooled over studies)."
  )
```

```{r gate}
# Structural gates on the centre of the AUC distribution and on the
# PTA curve at the MICs where it is neither 0% nor 100%. A mis-transcribed
# CL, dose or eGFR slope moves mean AUC24 by tens of percent.
pct_auc <- 100 * (mean(auc24$auc24) / published$auclast - 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(pct_auc) < 20,
  abs(pta$simulated[pta$mic == 0.25] - pta$published[pta$mic == 0.25]) < 15,
  abs(pta$simulated[pta$mic == 0.5] - pta$published[pta$mic == 0.5]) < 15
)
```

The pooled mean AUC24 of the virtual cohort is within a few percent of the
patient-weighted published mean, the per-arm SDs fall in the published
22.8-25.8 mg h/L range, and the pooled PTA curve follows Figure 4b across the
MIC range. The higher AUC24 of study 3 in the paper is not reproduced: in the
model the three arms differ only by covariates, whereas the paper's study 3
patients had a lower posterior mean CL (12.6 versus 16.6 and 16 L/h, Table 3)
that the covariates do not explain.

# Inter-occasion variability

Clearance varies between 24-h occasions with a CV of 13.6%. With seven
occasions the within-subject difference of log(CL) between two occasions has
an SD of sqrt(2 x 0.01833) = 0.191.

```{r iov}
iov_subj <- tibble(id = 1:200, WT = 70, CRCL = 58.64, STUDY_EXPAT = 0, STUDY_RDRN = 0)
iov_events <- iov_subj |>
  tidyr::crossing(OCC = 1:7) |>
  mutate(time = (OCC - 1) * 24 + 12, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(7)
sim_iov <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = iov_events) |>
  as.data.frame()
iov_sd <- sim_iov |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(d = log(cl[OCC == 2]) - log(cl[OCC == 1]), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(sd = sd(d)) |>
  pull(sd)
iov_sd
stopifnot(abs(iov_sd / sqrt(2 * 0.018327) - 1) < 0.25)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **eGFR effect.** Equation 3 multiplies CL by `1 + 0.008 x (eGFR - 58.64)`,
  i.e. a 0.8% change per mL/min/1.73 m^2. The Results prose describes the same
  coefficient as an absolute change ("CL increases 0.008 L/h when eGFR
  increases 1 mL/min/1.73 m^2"), which would be an effect about 15-fold
  smaller. The printed equation is implemented.
- **Number of occasions.** The paper defines every 24 h as an occasion but
  does not say how many occasions the data spanned. Seven are encoded (the
  first week of therapy), each sharing the single estimated IOV variance.
  Records with `OCC` outside 1-7 carry no IOV; the paper's own exposure
  simulation is restricted to the first 24 h (`OCC = 1`).
- **Study indicators.** Study 2 (Radboud UMC, Gieling 2020) is the reference
  stratum; `STUDY_EXPAT` (study 1) and `STUDY_RDRN` (study 3) select the other
  residual-error models and affect nothing else. For a new patient any stratum
  may be used; the choice only changes the simulated measurement noise.
- **Study differences in exposure.** The between-study differences in
  Figure 4 and Table 3 come from posterior samples of each patient's random
  effects, which are not published. They are not part of the population model
  and are not reproduced; only the pooled AUC24 and PTA are compared.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight and eGFR are drawn independently as
  log-normal variables matched to the Table 1 per-study median and IQR; the
  paper's simulation instead used the observed patients. The infusion duration
  of the paper's simulation is not stated; 30 min is used.
- **Figure 4b reading.** The PTA values at MICs other than 0.5 mg/L were read
  from Figure 4b by the maintainers (to about 2 percentage points). The figure
  caption gives 4200, 5900 and 3900 simulated patients for studies 1, 2 and 3,
  which does not match 100 samples x 42, 39 and 59 patients; the study 2 and
  study 3 counts appear swapped.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found in Europe PMC as of 2026-10-02.
